narration_lines: A rain gauge catches the rain. Its scale tells us how many millimetres of rain fell.
One millimetre of rain is one litre of water on every square metre.
Ten millimetres of rain gives ten litres on every square metre.
Rain can fall fast or slow. Fast rain is called heavy rain. Slow rain is light rain.
The rain adds up. The total is accumulated rainfall. First five, then ten more, then fifteen more.
A short heavy shower and a long gentle rain can give the same total.
When the news says one hundred millimetres, picture one hundred litres on every square metre.
Weather stations across Thailand measure the rain.
Next time it rains, we can read our own rain gauge.
